title: perf-benchmarking-sync-2026-06-09
body:
Perf & Benchmarking Sync - 2026-06-09

Attendees:
- Anya Patel (owner)
- Leo Zhang
- Maya Chen
- Ethan Brooks
- Jasmine Alvarez
- Joined late: Samir Rao (SRE)

Agenda:
1) Quick recap of last week's regressions
2) Nightly and canary test run results
3) Hypotheses and triage plan
4) Action items + owners

Summary:
- We observed p95 latency regressions on the redwood-v2-xl-8k-quant model across several configs during Friday's rolling canary. Baseline p95 for 512-token requests was ~210ms; canary showed ~360ms (+71%). P50 increased modestly from ~85ms to ~110ms. Throughput (tokens/sec) dropped ~18% under 16-concurrent-client load.
- Regression correlated temporally with runtime PR #1298 (kernel selection + batching changes) that was rolled to canary on 2026-06-05.

Recent test runs (summary of key numbers):
- Nightly bench (2026-06-08, batch=16, seq=512, model=redwood-v2-xl-8k-quant): p50=88ms, p95=220ms, Tput=18.6k tokens/sec
- Canary (2026-06-08, same config): p50=110ms, p95=360ms, Tput=15.3k tokens/sec
- Local microbench (previous runtime commit before PR1298): p50=86ms, p95=205ms, Tput=19.0k tokens/sec
- Canary run with KV-cache warm: p50=92ms, p95=330ms (suggests partial mitigation from cache but still regressed)
- Beam search / long seq (seq=2048) shows p95 spike to ~1.1s on canary vs 0.7s baseline.

What we traced so far:
- Heap allocations: small increase in allocator churn after PR1298; observed more frequent short-lived allocations in kernel selection path (Leo).
- Batching behavior: batch formation latency increased ~12ms on average for small requests, apparently due to tighter kernel compatibility checks before batching (Maya).
- Kernel fallbacks: on a subset of cases the runtime picks a fallback kernel with worse memory access pattern causing 2-3x op latency in inner loop (Ethan).
- No obvious GPU saturation (utilization similar between baseline and canary). SRE logs show no OOM or context-switch spikes.

Hypotheses:
1) Kernel selection checks in PR1298 are adding serialization/lock contention and preventing ideal batching — increases latency and reduces throughput.
2) Some kernel variants introduced by PR1298 are significantly slower for short sequences (edge-case instruction ordering).
3) Increased allocation churn causes GC-like pauses (Python-side scheduler interactions) that inflate tail latency for some requests.

Triage plan agreed:
- Reproduce minimal test case: pipeline to run single-node isolated reproducer that exercises kernel selection hotpath with controlled input distributions (owner: Leo, due: 2026-06-10).
- Bisect runtime changes between commit X (pre-PR1298) and current to isolate offending sub-commit (owner: Maya, due: 2026-06-11).
- Run microbench of each kernel variant with perf counters to identify slower kernels (owner: Ethan, due: 2026-06-11).
- Add lightweight instrumentation to measure time spent in kernel-selection and batching queue (owner: Anya, due: 2026-06-10).
- Canary rollback plan prepared: if we cannot identify a fix within 48h, we will rollback PR1298 on canary only (owner: Jasmine/SRE, runway: 48h).

Action items (concrete):
- Leo: Create isolated reproducer job + job config in perf infra (K8s job) and post logs to the perf channel. (due 2026-06-10)
- Maya: Bisect commits and post bisect log + candidate commit range to INF-4812. (due 2026-06-11)
- Ethan: Microbench kernel variants with nvprof/NSight and share hotspots. Attach perf counters to PR. (due 2026-06-11)
- Anya: Add telemetry to runtime to emit kernel-select latency metric and batching queue wait time; create dashboard. (due 2026-06-10)
- Jasmine / Samir (SRE): Standby for canary rollback; validate rollback playbook on staging. (complete dry-run by 2026-06-11)
- All: Add failing input examples and share in INF-4820. (ongoing)

Notes / troubleshooting logs pointers:
- Reproducer job: gs://redwood-perf/nightlies/2026-06-08/reproducer.tar.gz
- Canary logs (host: canary-3a): s3://redwood-logs/canary/2026-06-08/canary-3a.log
- Bisect tracking: JIRA INF-4812 (linked)
- Incident thread: #perf-regressions (Slack)

Risk assessment:
- User-visible impact: medium — tail latency regressions observable for latency-sensitive routes; revenue impact limited but could increase error budgets for some customers on dedicated pools.
- Time sensitivity: high — we want to stabilize canary before more rollouts and before end-of-week major deploy.

Next sync:
- Follow-up standup on 2026-06-10 10:00 PT to review reproducer results and telemetry spikes.
- If bisect identifies single bad commit, schedule hotfix PR and patch release window.

Open questions:
- Are there additional workloads (embeddings, long-streaming chat) that show similar regressions? (Action: all to drop short test inputs to perf infra and tag)
- Can we safely A/B kernel selection (old vs new) at runtime for a subset of requests to collect comparative telemetry? (Anya to prototype)

References:
- PR: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1298
- JIRA: INF-4812 (perf regression tracking), INF-4820 (failing inputs)

Session adjourned.
